references.text: Balaam is identified as the son of Beor, the same genealogical identification found in Numbers 22:5
Joshua mentions that Balak sent for Balaam, the son of Beor, to curse Israel
Balaam himself says that Balak brought him from Aram, from the mountains of the east, corresponding to Pethor by the river
The people of Israel multiplied and became numerous in Egypt, a description of the nation's growth that worried Balak
Locusts covered the whole land so that the ground could not be seen, similar imagery about covering the surface of the earth
Balaam, the son of Beor, was killed by the Israelites, the same person who was summoned in this verse
Micah reminds the people what Balak, king of Moab, planned and how Balaam answered
Peter's second letter mentions Balaam, the son of Bosor, who loved the wages of unrighteousness
The letter of Jude warns against those who have gone astray on the path of Balaam for profit
Revelation mentions the teaching of Balaam, which taught Balak to set a trap for the children of Israel
